Rashi on Shabbat 100a:10:1.hebrew: והא לא נח - חוץ לד', ואמאי אזלינן בתרה:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:10:1.english: But it did not come to rest - beyond four [cubits], and why do we follow it?

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:10:2.hebrew: שנח ע"ג משהו - שעמד קצת ואח"כ נתגלגל. והוא הדין אם אחזתן הרוח באויר ועכבתו מעט ואחר כך הכניסתו, דחשיב נמי הנחה אם בתוך ג' הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:10:2.english: That it came to rest upon something - That it stopped briefly and afterward rolled [back]. And the same law [applies] if the wind held it in the air and delayed it slightly, and afterward brought it in, for that too is considered a resting, if it is within three [handbreadths of the ground].

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:10:3.english: And the wind pushed it - While it [was] in the air.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:10:4.english: Seized it briefly - The wind detained it in its place briefly.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:11:1.hebrew: לרבנן - דפליגי עליה דר"ע בזורק מרה"י לרה"י ורה"ר באמצע, דלית להו קלוטה כמי שהונחה. לא תימא בתוך ג' מודו, אלא אפילו תוך ג' נמי צריך שינוח, ואם עבר רה"ר כולה, פטור. ונפקא מינה נמי לזורק ד' אמות, וכשבא לנוח והגיע לתוך ג' נזכר שגגתו עד שלא נח — פטור, כדאמרינן במתני' (דף קב.): עד שתהא תחלתו וסופו שגגה, ולא אמרינן עד שלא נזכר הוה ליה מונח:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:11:1.english: According to the Rabbis - Who disagree with Rabbi Akiva regarding one who throws [an object] from a private domain to a private domain with a public domain in between, as they do not hold [the principle that] something intercepted [in airspace] is as though it has come to rest. Do not say that within three [handbreadths of the ground] they concede [to Rabbi Akiva]; rather, even within three [handbreadths] it must also come to rest, and if it traversed the entire public domain [without coming to rest], he is exempt. And there is also a practical difference regarding one who throws [an object] four cubits [in a public domain], and as it was about to come to rest and reached within three [handbreadths of the ground], he remembered [that it was Shabbat, realizing] his unwitting transgression before it came to rest — he is exempt, as we say in the Mishnah (102a): "[He is not liable] unless its beginning and its end are unwitting," and we do not say that before he remembered, it was already [considered] at rest.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:1:1.hebrew: לאו היינו הנחתן - ואם נטלו משם, לאו עקירה היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:1:1.english: [That] is not their placement - And if one took it from there, it is not [considered] lifting.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:2:1.hebrew: שמן על גבי יין - לענין שבת, מחלוקת ר' יוחנן בן נורי ורבנן:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:2:1.english: Oil on wine - With regard to Shabbat, [it is] a dispute between Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri and the Rabbis.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:2:2.english: As we learned: oil - [Oil] of terumah.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:2:3.hebrew: שצף על גבי יין - של תרומה. משום הכי נקט טבול יום, משום דפוסל ואינו מטמא. הלכך, לא פסל אלא שמן בלבד, דלאו חיבור הוא למיהוי כחד. ואילו הוה טמא, הוה מטמא ליה לשמן, ושמן פסל ליה ליין:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:2:3.english: That floated on wine - [Oil and wine] of terumah. For this reason [the Mishnah] specified a tevul yom [one who immersed during the day], because he invalidates [terumah] but does not render [it] impure [so as to transmit impurity further]. Therefore, he invalidated only the oil alone, as [the oil and wine] are not [considered] a connection to be as one [entity]. Whereas if he had been impure [with a full impurity], he would have rendered the oil impure, and the oil would have invalidated the wine.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:2:4.hebrew: שניהם חיבור - דהוי כחד, ונפסל אף היין. ולענין שבת נמי, לרבנן הוה ליה כאגוז על גבי מים, ולרבי יוחנן הוה ליה כמים על גבי מים:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:2:4.english: The two [are] a connection - For they are like one [entity], and the wine is also invalidated. And with regard to Shabbat as well, according to the Rabbis it is like a nut on top of water, and according to Rabbi Yoḥanan [ben Nuri] it is like water on top of water.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:3:1.hebrew: וזרק לתוכה מחצלת - משום סיפא נקט ליה, דבעי למימר "חלקה במחצלת פטור", לאשמעי' דהנחת חפץ וסילוק מחיצה בהדדי פטור. והכא סילוק מחיצה, דזיל הכא ליכא ארבעה, וזיל הכא ליכא ד', דבצר ליה עובי מקום מחצלת:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:3:1.english: And one threw a mat into it - He mentioned it because of the latter clause, as he wanted to say, "[If] he divided it with a mat, he is exempt," to teach us that placing an object and removing a partition simultaneously [renders one] exempt. And here [there is] a removal of a partition, for go this way [and] there are not four [handbreadths], and go that way [and] there are not four [handbreadths], since the thickness of the mat's place diminishes it.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:3:2.english: All the more so a segment [of dirt] - For it is certainly a removal of the partition that nullifies it.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:3:3.hebrew: לרבי יוחנן מחצלת פשיטא ליה דלא מבטלה - דאי נמי אמרינן סילוק מחיצה והנחת חפץ כי הדדי פטור, הכא חייב, דלא מבטל ליה; הלכך, לאו סילוק מחיצה היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:3:3.english: According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, [regarding] a mat, it is obvious to him that it does not nullify [the partition] - For even if we say [that when] the removal of a partition and the placing of an object [occur] simultaneously he is exempt, here he is liable, because he does not nullify it; therefore, it is not [considered] a removal of the partition.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:4:1.hebrew: וזרק לתוכה - מרה"ר מידי דנייחא, כגון אבן או מים:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:4:1.english: And [one] threw into it - from the public domain, something that comes to rest, such as a stone or water.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:4:2.hebrew: חייב - ולא אמרינן, כיון דמלא הוא, לא הוי רה"י, דמבטל להו מחיצות:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:4:2.english: He is liable - And we do not say [that] since it is full, it is not a private domain, because [the water] nullifies the partitions.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:4:3.hebrew: מלאה פירות - פטור, דבטיל מחיצות, כאילו מלאוה עפר:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:4:3.english: Filled with fruit - he is exempt, because [the fruit] nullifies the partitions, as if they filled it with earth.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:4:4.english: This was also taught [in a baraita] - That water does not nullify a partition.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:4:5.hebrew: מן הים לאיסרטיא - מכרמלית לרה"ר פטור:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:4:5.english: From the sea to the street - From a karmelit to a public domain, [he is] exempt.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:4:7.hebrew: ר"ש אומר אם יש - בים במקום שזרק גומא מיוחדת לבדה, עמוקה עשרה ורחבה ד', רה"י לעצמה היא ולא הוי כשאר ים, אף על גב דים נמי עמוק הוא. וממילא שמעינן מדר"ש דמים לא מבטלי מחיצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:4:7.english: Rabbi Shimon says: If there is - in the sea, at the place where he threw [the object], a distinct pit unto itself, ten [handbreadths] deep and four [handbreadths] wide, it is a private domain unto itself and is not like the rest of the sea, even though the sea is also deep. And we automatically learn from Rabbi Shimon that water does not nullify a partition.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:7:1.hebrew: רבי מאיר ורבנן - דאיפליגו בחוקקים להשלים בפ"ק דיומא (דף יא:) ובעירובין (ד' יא:). לר"מ דאמר חוקקין להשלים במקו' שיש כדי לחוק, הכא חייב, דרואין החור כאלו הוא ארבע:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:7:1.english: Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis - Who disagreed regarding [the principle of] "one carves out to complete" in the first chapter of Yoma (11b) and in Eruvin (11b). According to Rabbi Meir, who says one carves out to complete in a place where there is enough [space] to carve, here he is liable, for we view the hole as though it were four [handbreadths wide].

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:8:1.hebrew: תל המתלקט - שהוא מדרון, והולך ומתלקט מעט מעט עד שמגביה י' מתוך ד"א, הרי הוא כאלו זקוף כולו והוי רה"י במקום גובהו, ואם זרק מרה"ר ונח על גביו, חייב. ודוקא נקט מתוך ד' אמות, דאי מתוך ה', הרי הוא כשאר רשות הרבים, דניחא תשמישתיה להילוך:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:8:1.english: A mound that gradually rises - That it is a slope, and it goes on rising little by little until it reaches a height of ten [handbreadths] over four cubits; behold, it is as though it were completely vertical, and it is a private domain at its high point, and if one threw [an object] from the public domain and it came to rest on top of it, he is liable. And [the Gemara] specifically stated "over four cubits," for if [it rose] over five [cubits], it is like the rest of the public domain, since its use for walking is convenient.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:8:2.hebrew: ונעשה מדרון לרה"ר - שהיה קרקע המבוי גבוה מקרקע רה"ר, והוצרך לשפע אצל פתחו לצד רה"ר. או שהיה שוה לרה"ר ונעשה מדרון לתוכה — שהיה רה"ר גבוה מקרקע המבוי, וכניסת המבוי נמי מן הפתח ולפנים גבוה כקרקע רה"ר ברחב אמה או חצי אמה, ואח"כ הוא נעשה מדרון לצד דופן האמצעי:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:8:2.english: And becomes an incline toward the public domain - For the ground of the alleyway was higher than the ground of the public domain, and it had to slope down at its entrance toward the public domain. Or [if] it was level with the public domain and became an incline toward its interior — [meaning] that the public domain was higher than the ground of the alleyway, and the entrance of the alleyway as well, from the opening inward, was as high as the ground of the public domain for a width of a cubit or half a cubit, and afterward it becomes an incline toward the middle wall.

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:8:3.english: That alleyway does not require a post - For that height at the side of the entrance is [considered] a partition, even though it slopes [gradually].

Rashi on Shabbat 100a:9:1.hebrew: זרק חוץ לד"א ונתגלגל כו' חייב - לא שנפל לארץ, דא"כ לא צריכא למימר, אלא שהרוח גלגלתהו מן האויר לתוך ד' אמות:
Rashi on Shabbat 100a:9:1.english: [If] one threw beyond four cubits and [it] rolled, etc., he is liable - [This does] not [mean] that it fell to the ground [beyond four cubits], for if so, it would not need to be stated; rather, [it means] that the wind rolled it from the air into within four cubits.

Tosafot on Shabbat 100a:10:1.hebrew: אחזתו הרוח משהו כו' - פי' שעיכבתו ע"ג קרקע או אפי' באויר, כדפי' בקונט', דחשיבה אחיזת הרוח כמונח על גבי משהו. ונראה דע"ג קרקע, אפי' לר' יהודה — דהיינו רבנן דקאמר רבא דצריך הנח' — מודה דלא בעינן, כדפי' לעיל (שבת דף פ.). ומיהו ק"ק דבסמוך מסקינן איפכא: דמתגלגל, כיון דאין סופו לנוח, לאו כמונח דמי; אבל האי, כיון דסופו לנוח, כמונח דמי! וחזר ר"י לפרש דודאי רבי יהודה סבר כר"ע, דקלוטה כמו שהונחה, היכא דבעי שתנוח שם, כי ההוא דפירקין; אבל בההוא דפרק בתרא דעירובין (ד' צז:), "היה קורא בספר", דלא בעי שתפול שם, בעי ר' יהודה הנחה על גבי משהו. ורבא קאמר דרבנן דר"ע לית להו קלוטה כמו שהונחה דמיא בשום מקום, אפי' רצונו שתנוח שם, אפילו תוך ג'. ולא ס"ל כברייתא דלעיל דקתני: "תוך ג' ד"ה חייב", אלא סבר כברייתא דהכא דקתני: "אחזתו הרוח משהו". ומתניתין נמי משמע דאיירי בנח משהו כדאוקי ר' יוחנן, דומיא דרישא דקתני: "תוך ד' אמות פטור", דאיירי בשנח, דאי לאו הכי אמאי מיפטר? ורב חלקיה בר טוביה דאמר לעיל: "תוך שלשה ד"ה חייב", מוקי מתניתין בדלא נח, ורישא דקתני פטור מיירי כגון שפסק כחו ומחמת הרוח נתגלגל חוץ לארבע:
Tosafot on Shabbat 100a:10:1.english: "The wind seized it briefly, etc." - Explanation: That [the wind] held it back on the ground, or even in the air, as Rashi explained, for the wind's seizing [it] is considered like resting atop something. And it appears that on the ground, even Rabbi Yehudah — who is [the opinion of] the Rabbis of whom Rava said that [the object] requires resting [atop something] — concedes that we do not require [it], as we explained above (Shabbat 80a). However, it is somewhat difficult, for shortly below [the Gemara] concludes the opposite: that a rolling [object], since it will not ultimately come to rest, is not considered as having come to rest; whereas this [object within three handbreadths], since it will ultimately come to rest, is considered as having come to rest! Therefore, Ri retracted [that explanation] and explained that certainly Rabbi Yehudah holds like Rabbi Akiva that [an object] intercepted [in the airspace] is as though it had been placed down, where [the thrower] wants it to rest there, like that [case] in our chapter; however, in that [case] in the last chapter of Eruvin (97b), "One was reading from a scroll," where he does not want it to fall there, Rabbi Yehudah requires resting atop something. And Rava is saying that the Rabbis [who dispute] Rabbi Akiva do not hold that [an object] intercepted [in the airspace] is considered as though it had been placed down in any situation — even [where] his desire is that it rest there, even within three [handbreadths]. And [Rava] does not hold like the baraita above, which teaches: "Within three [handbreadths], all agree he is liable"; rather, he holds like the baraita here, which teaches: "If the wind seized it briefly." And our Mishnah also implies that it is speaking of where it rested briefly, as Rabbi Yoḥanan established, similar to the first clause, which teaches: "[If he threw it] within four cubits [and it rolled beyond four cubits], he is exempt," which is speaking of where it rested [within four cubits], for if not so, why would he be exempt? And Rav Ḥilkiah bar Toviyah, who said above: "Within three [handbreadths], all agree he is liable," establishes our Mishnah as [speaking of] where it did not rest, and the first clause, which teaches "he is exempt," is speaking of a case such as where his force ceased and because of the wind it rolled beyond four [cubits].

Tosafot on Shabbat 100a:4:1.hebrew: פירות מבטלי מחיצתא - וא"ת: ומ"ש מדבילה שמינה, דאמרינן לעיל דלא מבטלי, ואביי דהכא אית ליה שינויא דבדבילה שמינה שנו — כדאמר בפ"ק (דף ז:): "זימנין משני ליה בכותל דלית ביה חור ובדבילה שמינה כו'"? וי"ל, דדבילה אינה עומדת כל כך להתבטל שם בכותל, כמו שרגילין לבטל פירות בבור כעין תבואה. אי נמי: דבילה דבר מועט הוא ולא מבטלא, אבל בור מלא פירות או חציו מבטל רה"י; וה"ה דגרעין אחד או דבר מועט לא מבטל רה"י. וא"ת: היכי ממעטי הני פירות, והא אמר בפרק חלון (עירובין עח:): כל דבר הניטל בשבת אינו ממעט? ואפי' אי איירי הכא בטבל שאין ניטל בשבת, מ"מ כיון דניטל מן התורה, הזורק לתוכו אמאי פטור? ואומר ר"י, דמן התורה ממעט כל דבר, ואפילו הניטל, ומדרבנן הוא דגזרו דדבר הניטל אינו ממעט. ולהכי לא קאמר "מותר לזרוק בתוכו", אלא קאמר "הזורק לתוכו פטור", משמע דאיסורא דרבנן איכא. ואפילו בחריץ שבין שתי חצרות אמרו דדבר הניטל אינו ממעט, אע"ג דהוי לקולא דלא אסרי אהדדי. אבל ק"ק, דבפרק חלון (שם) מייתי על בית שמילאוהו תבן, דהוי לענין אהל דאורייתא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 100a:4:1.english: Fruit eliminates the partition - And if you ask: How is this different from a fat fig-cake, [regarding which] we said earlier that it does not nullify [the hole's depth] — and Abaye here has the resolution that [the Mishnah] taught [its ruling] regarding a fat fig-cake, as it says in the first chapter (7b): "Sometimes he resolves it as a wall that has no hole, and regarding a fat fig-cake, etc."? And one can answer that a fig-cake is not meant to remain nullified there in the wall as much as people are accustomed to nullify fruit in a pit, such as grain. Alternatively: a fig-cake is a small thing and does not nullify [the domain], whereas a pit full of fruit — or half-full — nullifies a private domain; and the same applies that a single kernel or a small thing does not nullify a private domain. And if you ask: How do these fruits reduce [the pit's depth], when it says in Perek Chalon (Eruvin 78b): Anything that may be moved on Shabbat does not reduce [a partition]? And even if [our Gemara] here is speaking of tevel [untithed produce], which may not be moved on Shabbat, nevertheless, since it may be moved by Torah law, why is one who throws into it exempt? And Ri says that by Torah law anything reduces [it], even something that may be moved, and it is by Rabbinic decree that they decreed that something which may be moved does not reduce [it]. And therefore [Abaye] does not say "it is permitted to throw into it," rather he says "one who throws into it is exempt," implying that there is a Rabbinic prohibition. And even regarding a trench between two courtyards, they said that something which may be moved does not reduce [it], even though it results in a leniency, that [the courtyards] do not prohibit one another. However, it is somewhat difficult, for in Perek Chalon (ibid.) [the Gemara] cites [this principle] regarding a house that they filled with straw, which is with respect to ohel [tent-impurity] of Torah law:

Tosafot on Shabbat 100a:6:1.hebrew: והא לא נח - וא"ת: מאי פריך? והתניא לעיל (שבת ד' צז.): תוך ג' ד"ה חייב, אע"ג דלא נח! ואין נראה לומר דאתוך ד' אמות קאי: אמאי פטור? הא לא נח, וא"כ כשנח אחר כך חוץ לארבע יתחייב; דהא (מתניתין) נמי הכי משמע, דאחוץ לד' אמות פריך אמאי חייב. וי"ל דפריך לרבא, דאמר: תוך שלשה לרבנן בעי הנחה ע"ג משהו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 100a:6:1.english: And it did not come to rest - And if you ask: What is [the Gemara] asking? For was it not taught in a baraita above (Shabbat 97a): Within three [handbreadths], everyone agrees he is liable, even though it did not come to rest! And it does not seem [correct] to say that [the Gemara] is referring to within four cubits: why is he exempt? [For] it did not come to rest [there], and if so, when it subsequently comes to rest beyond four [cubits] he should be liable; for (the Mishnah) also implies thus, that [the Gemara] is asking about beyond four cubits: why is he liable? And one can answer that [the Gemara] is asking according to Rava, who said [that] within three [handbreadths], according to the Rabbis, it requires coming to rest on top of something.

Tosafot on Shabbat 100a:7:1.hebrew: והלכה ונחה בחור כל שהוא כו' - בחור מפולש איירי, והאי חוקקין להשלים היינו לשוויה מקום ד', כדפי' בפ"ק (דף ז:):
Tosafot on Shabbat 100a:7:1.english: "And it went and came to rest in a hole of any size," etc. - [The Gemara] is speaking of a hole that goes all the way through [the wall], and this [statement], "one carves out to complete," means to make it a place of four [handbreadths], as I explained in the first chapter (7b).
